translationRepairs: Under the Tianqi emperor he rose to Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent before retiring to mourn a parent.
Under the Tianqi emperor he rose through office to Supervisor of the Household of the Heir Apparent before going home to mourn a parent.
詹事 is the Supervisor of the Household of the Heir Apparent (head of the Supervisorate), not "Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent".
In the third year of Chongzhen he was recalled and made Vice Minister of Rites.
In the third year of Chongzhen he was recalled and made Right Vice Minister of Rites.
禮部右侍郎 is specifically the Right Vice Minister; "Right" was omitted.

That winter the court nominated candidates for the Grand Secretariat; Yingxiong's reputation was too slight to make the list, yet a special edict raised him to Minister of Rites and Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion, and he entered the privy council alongside He Wuyao.

In the winter of the sixth year the court nominated candidates for the Grand Secretariat; Yingxiong's reputation was too slight to make the list, yet a special edict raised him to Minister of Rites and Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion, and he entered the privy council alongside He Wuyao.
六年冬 gives the year (Chongzhen 6); "That winter" drops it and wrongly ties the event to the previous date.
That winter the court dispatched an envoy to recall Yingxiong.
In the winter of the fifteenth year the court dispatched an envoy to recall Yingxiong.
十五年冬 specifies the fifteenth year; "That winter" loses the date.
(Cai Guoyong, Fan Fuchun, Fang Fengnian, Zhang Sizhi, and others)〉
(Cai Guoyong, Fan Fucui, Fang Fengnian, Zhang Sizhi, and others)〉
範復粹 reads Fan Fucui (粹 cuì), not "Fan Fuchun".
After serving as a Hanlin Bachelor he rose to Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
After serving as a Hanlin Bachelor he rose to Junior Supervisor of the Household of the Heir Apparent.
少詹事 is the Junior Supervisor of the Household of the Heir Apparent, not "Junior Mentor".
In the fifth year of Chongzhen he was made Vice Minister of Rites.
In the fifth year of Chongzhen he was made Right Vice Minister of Rites.
禮部右侍郎 is specifically the Right Vice Minister.
In the forty-third year, during famine in Henan, he asked to retain grain reserves for relief and to convert tribute grain to cash payments; both requests were approved.
In the forty-third year, during famine in Henan, he asked to retain grain reserves for relief and to convert tribute grain to cash payments; the throne merely acknowledged both requests.
皆報聞 means the memorials were merely acknowledged ("noted"), not granted.
In the first year of Tianqi he was made vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review.
In the first year of Tianqi he was made Aide of the Court of Judicial Review.
大理寺丞 is the Aide (assistant) of the Court of Judicial Review, not its vice minister (少卿).
In the third year he asked leave to complete mourning for a parent.
In the third year he asked leave to go home and care for his aged parent.
終養 means retiring to care for a living parent until the end of their life, not mourning.
Wei Zhongxian's faction recommended him and a forged edict ordered the Ministry of Personnel to promote him, but Zhifa was in mourning and refused to serve.
Wei Zhongxian's faction recommended him and a forged edict ordered the Ministry of Personnel to promote him, but Zhifa was caring for his parent and would not come out.
方養親 means he was caring for his parent, not in mourning.
In the fifth year of Chongzhen he was recalled as vice minister of Shuntian Prefecture and promoted to Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
In the fifth year of Chongzhen he was recalled as Aide of Shuntian Prefecture and promoted to Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
順天府丞 is the Aide (vice prefect) of Shuntian Prefecture, not a vice minister.
Lecturer Xiang Yu accused Zhifa of controlling examinations and appointments, favoring his son-in-law Ren Jun while suppressing Cheng Yong.
Lecturer Xiang Yu accused Zhifa of controlling examinations and appointments, favoring his relative by marriage Ren Jun while suppressing Cheng Yong.
兒女姻 denotes a relative linked by the marriage of their children, not a son-in-law.
Soon Vice Minister Cao Quan of the Court of Judicial Review exposed Ying'en's bribery, implicating Zhifa.
Soon Cao Quan, Deputy of the Court of Judicial Review, exposed Ying'en's bribery, implicating Zhifa.
大理寺副 is a Deputy (寺副) of the Court of Judicial Review, a low post, not its vice minister (少卿).
In the first year of Chongzhen he became Director of the Imperial Academy, then Junior Mentor while retaining charge of the Academy.
In the first year of Chongzhen he became Director of the Imperial Academy, then Junior Supervisor of the Household of the Heir Apparent while retaining charge of the Academy.
少詹 abbreviates 少詹事, the Junior Supervisor of the Household of the Heir Apparent, not "Junior Mentor".
That winter the capital region was invaded; he submitted plans for defense, garrison duty, and relief.
In the tenth month, in winter, the capital region was invaded; he submitted plans for defense, garrison duty, and relief.
冬十月 gives the tenth month; "That winter" drops it.
In Chongzhen 9 he entered the secretariat, was made Junior Mentor, and took leave to go home.
In Chongzhen 9 he entered the secretariat, was repeatedly raised to Junior Preceptor, and took leave to go home.
少傅 is the Junior Preceptor, distinct from Junior Mentor (少師); 累加 means repeated advancement.
He was appointed subprefectural judge in Laizhou.
He was appointed prefectural judge of Laizhou.
推官 is a prefectural judge (Laizhou was a prefecture), not a subprefectural judge.
Public opinion would not bear him, and he soon retired on grounds of final parental mourning.
Public opinion would not tolerate him, and he soon left to care for his aged parent.
終養 means retiring to care for a living parent, not mourning.
The next eighth month he was made Vice Minister of Rites and Eastern Lodge Grand Secretary, joining state deliberations.
The next eighth month he was made Left Vice Minister of Rites and Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion, joining state deliberations.
禮部左侍郎 is the Left Vice Minister; 東閣 is the Eastern Pavilion, used consistently elsewhere in this chapter.
When Yang Xianming's verification memorial arrived, Guoguan fought hard to clear Shi Kun—yet sixty thousand taels in gold could not be hidden.
When Yang Xianming's verification memorial arrived it strove to clear Shi Kun, yet sixty thousand taels could not be concealed;
力為褷解 is the subject of 顯名核疏 (Yang Xianming's report), not Guoguan; 金 here is a silver-tael sum, not "gold".
He pointed to Martial Tranquility Marquis Li Guorui.
He pointed to Li Guorui, Marquis of Wuqing.
武清侯 is the Marquis of Wuqing (a place name), not "Martial Tranquility Marquis".
Guorui was a grandson on Empress Dowager Xiaoding's side—the emperor's maternal great-grandmother's kin.
Guorui was a grandson of Empress Dowager Xiaoding's elder brother; hers was the family of the emperor's great-grandmother.
兄孫 is a brother's grandson; Xiaoding was the Chongzhen emperor's paternal great-grandmother, not maternal.
Jiading Duke Zhou Kui, a relation, interceded for him.
Zhou Kui, Earl of Jiading, who was related to him, interceded on his behalf.
嘉定伯 is the Earl (伯), not Duke, of Jiading.
Xu Yunzhen of Wei, chief of the military commission, Fu Yongchun of Personnel, and others misread the throne; their report was mild—retirement or idle post.
Xu Yunzhen, Duke of Wei, in charge of the Chief Military Commission, Minister of Personnel Fu Yongchun, and others misread the throne; their report was mild—retirement or idle post.
魏國公 is the Duke of Wei; 掌都督府 heads the Chief Military Commission.
He soon became vice director at the Right Review Court.
He soon became Right Aide of the Court of Judicial Review.
大理右寺丞 is the Right Aide of the Court of Judicial Review (大理寺), not a "Right Review Court".
He served as Minister of Ceremonies and Nanjing transmission commissioner, became vice minister of Works, then moved to Revenue.
He served as Chief Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Nanjing Transmission Commissioner, became vice minister of Works there, then moved to Revenue.
太常卿 is the Chief Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, not "Minister of Ceremonies".
Days later Guoxiang became Minister of Rites; with Yang Sichang, Fang Fengnian, Cai Guoyong, and Fan Fuchun he entered the Eastern Pavilion as grand secretary.
Days later Guoxiang became Minister of Rites; with Yang Sichang, Fang Fengnian, Cai Guoyong, and Fan Fucui he entered the Eastern Pavilion as grand secretary.
範復粹 reads Fan Fucui (粹 cuì), not "Fan Fuchun".
He died in office in the sixth month of Chongzhen 13 and was posthumously made Grand Guardian with the temple name Wenge.
He died in office in the sixth month of Chongzhen 13 and was posthumously made Grand Guardian with the posthumous name Wenke.
謚文恪 is a posthumous name (謚), not a temple name; 恪 reads kè.
Fan Fuchun came from Huang County.
Fan Fucui came from Huang County.
範復粹 reads Fan Fucui (粹 cuì), not "Fan Fuchun".
His first appointment was as investigating censor in Kaifeng Prefecture.
His first appointment was as prefectural judge of Kaifeng Prefecture.
推官 is a prefectural judge, not an investigating censor.

He also said, "Yuan Chonghuan's merit lay in securing all Liaodong, yet Court of Imperial Sacrifices Director Dong Maozhong slandered him as shielded by traitor factions—his position was wildly absurd."

He also said, "Yuan Chonghuan's merit lay in securing all Liaodong, yet Dong Maozhong, Chief Minister of the Seals Office, slandered him as shielded by traitor factions—his position was wildly absurd."
尚寶卿 heads the Seals Office (尚寶司), not the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
He rose from right assistant director to left vice minister in the Court of the Great Canon.
He rose from Right Aide to Left Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review.
大理右寺丞…左少卿 are posts in the Court of Judicial Review (大理寺), not "the Court of the Great Canon".
After Guo Guan’s dismissal in the sixth month of Chongzhen 13, Fuchun became chief minister.
After Guoguan's dismissal in the sixth month of Chongzhen 13, Fucui became chief minister.
國觀 is Xue Guoguan ("Guoguan", not "Guo Guan"); 復粹 reads Fucui.
Are there those who slight the scholar-official class yet seek a Gao Yao, a Qi, a Ji, or a Xie among the yellow-robed palace eunuchs?"
Are there those who slight the scholar-official class yet seek a Gao Yao, a Kui, a Ji, or a Xie among the yellow-robed palace eunuchs?"
夔 is Kui, the music master of Shun, not "Qi".
In Chongzhen 11 he went from heir-apparent tutor to Vice Minister of Rites and mentor of Hanlin bachelors.
In Chongzhen 11 he went from Supervisor of the Household of the Heir Apparent to Vice Minister of Rites and instructor of the Hanlin bachelors.
詹事 is the Supervisor of the Household of the Heir Apparent, not a tutor.
His grandfather Xiao, a Wanli-era censor who oversaw anti-Wokou levies, died in Korea and was posthumously made Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
His grandfather Xiao, a Wanli-era censor who supervised the army campaigning against the Japanese, died in Korea and was posthumously made Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
監征倭軍 is supervising the army against the Japanese (not levies); 光祿卿 heads the Court of Imperial Entertainments, not Imperial Sacrifices.
In Chongzhen he was junior grand secretary, headed the Hanlin Academy, and lectured before the throne.
In Chongzhen he rose to Junior Supervisor of the Household of the Heir Apparent, headed the Hanlin Academy, and lectured before the throne.
少詹事 is the Junior Supervisor of the Household of the Heir Apparent, not a "junior grand secretary".
In Chongzhen 15, rewarded for quelling Shandong bandits, he became junior tutor to the heir apparent and Minister of Revenue in the Hall of Military Glory.
In Chongzhen 15, rewarded for quelling Shandong bandits, he became Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Minister of Revenue in the Hall of Military Glory.
太子少保 is the Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, not a "junior tutor".
After the Hanlin academy he served as reviser.
From Hanlin bachelor he was appointed Reviewer.
由庶吉士授檢討: he was a Hanlin bachelor and then appointed Hanlin Reviewer (檢討).

Hardly had Chen Yan stepped down when the Jili-Liaodong governor Wang Yongji memorialized in fierce condemnation, demanding the full penalty of the law; the supervising secretaries Wang Weixiao and Sun Chengyze joined the attack with equal vehemence.

Hardly had Chen Yan stepped down when Wang Yongji, Supreme Commander of Jizhou and Liaodong, memorialized in fierce condemnation, demanding the full penalty of the law; the supervising secretaries Wang Weixiao and Sun Chengze joined the attack with equal vehemence.
孫承澤 is Sun Chengze (not "Chengyze"); 薊遼總督 is the Supreme Commander of Jizhou-Liaodong.
Wei Zaode answered with a single phrase—"know shame"—and went on to recount how he had held Tongzhou for eleven years.
Wei Zaode answered with a single phrase—"know shame"—and went on to recount his merit in defending Tongzhou in the eleventh year.
十一年守通州功 is his merit in defending Tongzhou in Chongzhen 11, not "for eleven years".
Li Jiantai withdrew and at once asked that the former censor Wei Zhen be restored to office;
Li Jiantai withdrew and at once asked that the former censor Wei Zhengu be restored to office;
故御史衛楨固官: the name is 衛楨固 (Wei Zhengu); 官 is "office".
he named the jinshi Ling Ting Director of the Bureau of Appointments and army supervisor;
he had the jinshi Ling Jiong made Secretary of the Bureau of Operations and army supervisor;
駉 reads jiōng (Ling Jiong); 職方主事 is a Secretary of the Bureau of Operations, not a Director of Appointments.
Chief Commandant of the Horse Wan Wei offered sacrificial oxen at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
The imperial son-in-law Wan Wei, Commandant-escort, offered a special sacrifice at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
駙馬都尉 is the title of an imperial son-in-law (Commandant-escort), not "Chief Commandant of the Horse".

Grand secretaries, heads of the Five Offices and Six Ministries, Censorate chiefs, and capital military commanders stood by; the Court of Imperial Entertainments led the ceremony while censors enforced decorum.

Grand secretaries, heads of the Five Offices and Six Ministries, Censorate chiefs, and capital military commanders stood by; the Court of State Ceremonial led the ceremony while censors enforced decorum.
鴻臚 is the Court of State Ceremonial, not the Court of Imperial Entertainments (光祿).
Xue Yingxiong was rigid and brutal; Chen Zhifa was treacherous and jealous.
Wang Yingxiong was rigid and brutal; Zhang Zhifa was treacherous and jealous.
應熊 is Wang Yingxiong and 至發 is Zhang Zhifa, subjects of this chapter; the surnames Xue and Chen are wrong.
Zhou Guo'an was secretive and cruel, mimicking Wen Tiren in everything, until the dynasty's vital breath was all but spent.
Xue Guoguan was secretive and cruel, mimicking Wen Tiren in everything, until the dynasty's vital breath was all but spent.
國觀 is Xue Guoguan, subject of this chapter, not "Zhou Guo'an".
